title: chat-compat: resilient streaming chunking, stop-array normalization, and tool-call metadata envelope
author: Leah Park
release_notes: Stabilizes OpenAI /v1/chat.completions streaming behavior: normalizes stop to an array, guarantees logprob envelope is emitted consistently during partial streaming, and wraps function/tool call metadata in a stable event envelope. Backwards-compatible: legacy single-string stop values accepted and normalized. Fixes several edge cases where streaming chunks split token logprobs or omitted final function call payload.
description:
Motivation: customer integrations observed intermittent incompatibilities when using Redwood's OpenAI-compat endpoint for /v1/chat.completions. Problems included (1) callers sending stop as a single string vs array, (2) streaming chunks that split token-level logprobs causing consumers to miss logprob metadata, and (3) inconsistent placement/framing of function/tool-call payloads in the stream. This PR converges the compatibility surface so integrations get deterministic envelopes for tooling and logprobs, and normalizes params for easier client code.

Scope and approach: - Normalize incoming `stop` to an ordered array early in request validation and propagate canonical stop semantics into runtime routing. - Introduce a compact "stream-envelope" framing for ephemeral streaming events: {type, data, meta} where type in [delta, logprob, function_call_start, function_call_end, done]. Implementation keeps human readable JSON per-chunk but adds a single-char prefix for alignment detection to help clients resync on partial TCP chunks. - Ensure token-level logprobs are emitted as discrete logprob events whenever a KV-cache flush or chunk boundary would otherwise split values; this avoids partial-token loss. - Formalize function/tool call handshake: emit function_call_start with provisional metadata, stream tool outputs as delta events, then emit function_call_end with final structured payload. - Maintain backward compatibility for simple consumers: if client requests legacy framing (compat_mode: legacy), the server will still emit plain-delta chunks for text only responses.

Checklist: - [x] normalize stop param and add unit tests - [x] add streaming envelope encoder/decoder - [x] add e2e tests simulating chunk boundary splits - [x] add SDK parser update (TS) and docs - [x] perf smoke test on dedicated pool - [x] audit and update observability traces/metrics

Related work: ENG-1189 (streaming resilience), ENG-1212 (openai-compat parity), incident SUP-8721 referenced a customer outage.

Implementation notes: commits implement a small deterministic prefix ("~\n") per payload to help the client locate JSON boundaries after network partial reads; we debated binary framing but decided on a minimal ASCII prefix to preserve existing text-streaming client simplicity. The canonical stop normalization is applied in packages/redwood-api/src/inputValidation.ts and packages/openai-compat/src/paramNormalizer.ts. The streaming envelope lives in packages/openai-compat/src/streamingEnvelope.ts and the runtime emitter uses runtime/stream-router to decide when to break and emit logprob events.

Tests: unit tests cover normalizations and envelope conformance; e2e covers canary rollout using a dedicated test pool with artificially delayed TCP chunks to reproduce splits.

Rollout plan: merged to main, canary on dedicated cluster (10% traffic) for 48h, metrics to watch: stream-fragment-recover-rate, function-call-missing, avg-latency-95.

Backwards compatibility: legacy consumers unaffected; new behavior is opt-out via compat_mode=legacy if downstream parsing cannot be upgraded.

Documentation: updated docs/openai-compat.md with examples for new envelope and SDK change notes.

CI notes: initial CI run failed a flaky e2e test (chat-stream.spec.ts) which was fixed by increasing the TCP chunk jitter simulation timeout; final run passed.

notes_for_release: Opt-in backwards compat: compat_mode=legacy restores previous plain streaming framing.
New stable framing: clients should update stream parsers to handle logprob and function_call envelopes if they need token-level metadata.
Stop param: single string values will be normalized to [string] under the hood; no client change required unless relying on strict equality checks.
